But content follows the job, not the author; the same person writing a model file and a preprocessing notebook would also write dense linear algebra in one and string munging in the other. Go find a tell that survives the job difference: variable naming style, import ordering, whether they use `"` or `'`, how they comment. Which of those actually differs between the two files?

conversation.speaker: SAGE
conversation.text: Upon reviewing the code, I notice that "data_preprocessing.ipynb" uses triple quotes (`"""`) for docstrings, whereas "model.py" uses single quotes (`'') for string literals and comments. This difference in quoting style caught my attention as something more nuanced than just job-related differences.

conversation.speaker: Claude
conversation.text: Careful — you compared *docstrings* in one file to *string literals* in the other, and those are different slots; a single author uses `"""` for docstrings and `'` for literals all the time, so that difference might be the slot rather than the hand. Give me a fair test: run `grep -o "'" <file> | wc -l` and `grep -o '"' <file> | wc -l` on each, and paste the four raw numbers along with the exact paths you ran them on.
